name: Fix stored XSS in dynamic block render callback
query:
I built a dynamic callout block for my plugin; its PHP render_callback is just `return '
' . $attributes['message'] . '
';`. During review we noticed an editor user could save `` as the message and it fires for every visitor viewing the post. Please make the block render safely.
expected_behavior: Locate the callout block's render_callback registered via register_block_type() and confirm the message attribute reaches the returned markup unescaped
Treat block attributes as user input: the declared type in block.json validates shape but does not sanitize HTML or JavaScript
Sanitize the message attribute before use with sanitize_text_field(), guarding with isset() and a default value per the skill's pattern
Escape the value for its HTML context with esc_html() in the string the callback returns

If any secondary attribute (e.g. a level or tone) is rendered into the class or an attribute context, constrain it with an allowlist plus sanitize_key()/sanitize_html_class() and get_block_wrapper_attributes(), or escape with esc_attr()/esc_url() as the context requires
If the block is changed to allow rich markup in the message, constrain the stored value with wp_kses_post() instead of raw storage
Re-check the whole callback so no attribute is concatenated into the returned markup without sanitization and escaping
Confirm the fix against the reported payload: the onerror injection no longer executes and renders as inert text
success_criteria: The render_callback sanitizes the message attribute (e.g. sanitize_text_field()) before it is used
Rendered output escapes the attribute for its context (esc_html() for HTML content)
The reported onerror payload never executes; text-only or explicitly allowlisted rich-content behavior is preserved.
No block attribute is concatenated into the returned markup without sanitization and escaping
Any attribute placed in a class or attribute context is constrained (allowlist with sanitize_key()/sanitize_html_class()) or escaped (esc_attr()/esc_url())
The block still registers via register_block_type() and renders its intended callout markup, so functionality is preserved
